content:
A piece for flute made of 2 interleaved chromatic scales. Structure the line of the flute as two interleaved chromatic lines starting from low D going up. The two lines are identical, but the first one is played in twelfth-harmonics so that the lowest D will be a high A, then D# will be A# and so on. The interleaving idea is that an increasing number of notes of the second line are little by little inserted in between the notes of the first line: first, 0 notes are inserted between the first and second note of the first line; then 1 note of the second line is inserted between the second and third note of the first line; then 2 notes, then 3, 4, 5, etc. I can control starting pitch, offset interval and number of total notes

Reference for this request (every pitch is sounding pitch, in midicents):

# Woodwinds (flutes, oboes, clarinets, bassoons)

One note at a time (except multiphonics), shaped by the breath: a note can
swell and fade while it sounds ("dyn": "p<f>p"). Microtones are played with
special fingerings: write the exact midicents; fast microtonal passages are
harder and the colour changes from note to note.

breath: the player needs silences to breathe. A phrase without a gap can last
about 5–15 s depending on instrument, register and dynamic; leave a gap of at
least 300–500 ms between phrases.

techniques:
- legato (slurred): no slurs in this score; let each note last until the next onset
- tonguing: every separate note is tongued; single tonguing up to about 8 notes per second, double and triple tonguing faster (easiest on the flutes)
- staccato: "art": "staccato"; accent: "art": "accent"; tenuto: "art": "tenuto"
- flutter-tonguing, a rolled r or throat growl: "art": "tremolo" with "text": "flz."
- trill: "art": "trill"
- harmonics: "art": "harmonic" on the sounding pitch (see each instrument's Harmonics)
- multiphonics, several notes from one fingering: a chord of 2–4 notes with "text": "multiphonic"; the pitches depend on the fingering and are approximate; soft to medium dynamics, held notes
- key clicks, the keys struck without blowing: "head": "cross" with "text": "key clicks"; very soft, pitch approximate
- air sound, breath with little or no pitch: "text": "air"
- bends and glissando: "gliss" on the note; how far depends on the instrument
- vibrato on / off: "text": "vib." / "senza vib."
- dynamics: crescendo and diminuendo on one note work in every register

# Flute

register: 6000–9600
- 6000–6700 low: soft, breathy and dark; cannot play loud; easily covered by the ensemble
- 6700–8400 middle: clear and flexible, the most agile register
- 8400–9600 high: bright and easily loud; very soft playing gets hard above about 9100
expanded_register: 5900 only with a B foot joint (most professional flutes have one); 9600–10000 very high: piercing, loud, hard to play softly; up to about 10300 in contemporary solo writing.
transposing: no
techniques: the woodwind techniques (woodwinds/_family.md), plus:
- the most agile woodwind: fast scales, arpeggios and wide leaps; double and triple tonguing for very fast repeated notes
- bends of about a quarter-tone to a semitone ("gliss": ±50 to ±100)
- whistle tones, very soft high partials: "text": "whistle tones"
- jet whistle, a loud rush of air sweeping in pitch: "text": "jet whistle"
- tongue pizzicato, a short percussive pop: "text": "pizz."
- tongue ram, embouchure closed with the tongue: "text": "tongue ram"; sounds about 1100 below the fingered note, so write that sounding pitch
- uses air fast in the low register: shorter phrases there

## Harmonics
Overblowing a low fingering gives its partials. Partial n sounds at the
fingered note + 1200·log2(n): 2 → +1200, 3 → +1902, 4 → +2400, 5 → +2786,
6 → +3102. From fingerings 6000–6700; from 6000: 7200 7902 8400 8786 9102.
The real pitch can differ by a few cents from these values. Harmonics are
softer and more veiled than the normal notes of the same pitch; very high
partials played very softly are the whistle tones.

Write the sounding pitch with "art": "harmonic".

content:
OK. Algorithm saved as algorithms/gervasoni.js and sent to Max (gervasoni).
Parameters (now a panel in Max):
  start: slider 1200..12700 mc = 3800
  offset: slider 0..600 mc = 100
  notes: slider 8..64 = 20
  tempo: slider 60..480 ms = 150
  phrase: slider 2..16 = 8
  gap: slider 300..2000 ms = 600
Checked in 13 runs (every slider at its minimum and maximum, every option).
Score at the declared values (40 notes, 1 ms):
voice 1 (Flute): 40 notes in 40 chords, 0-5988 ms, pitch 3800-5800

Sent: two interleaved chromatic lines from the same start — line 1 overblown to its 3rd partial (so D2 sounds A4, D#2 → A#4), line 2 at its fingered pitch — with one more note of line 2 inserted between successive notes of line 1 each time, plus controls for the start pitch, the offset interval and total notes.
